findings.title: The chain end step's basic content directs a status read without the chained command's --chain-ran/--chain-head flags
findings.recommendation: Today CHAIN_END_STEP is read whole before the read, and its may_run bullet tells a chained command's closing step to read the status with `--chain-ran "<next>" --chain-head "<head>"` added. In the drafted basic content the read is plain `orbit status --change "<name>" --json`, and the flags appear only in references/chain-end-step.md, which is opened AFTER that read returns configured: true. orbit-engine-gates says a call without the two flags never matches `no-progress`, so a chained command that wrote no run record (a failed external launch) can be granted again from the flagless read, which RG0 forbids under a chain setting. Put the flags back in the basic content, or send a chained arrival to the reference before the read, and state that half in the orbit-conventions delta's list of what the basic content holds (spec.md:41-46).

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Add one clause to CHAIN_END_STEP_BASIC's read sentence: a command a chain ran adds `--chain-ran "<next>" --chain-head "<head>"` (the next and head the previous read reported, a null head written as null). Add it to the delta's basic-content list and re-measure the size table.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Have the basic content say: when this command was itself run by a chain, read references/chain-end-step.md BEFORE the status read and follow it. The basic content stays small, and the delta names the routing.

findings.title: The new closure 'a command a chain arrives at meets no tag its own body does not explain' is false on day one
findings.recommendation: The sentence covers every command a chain arrives at, but: (1) archive is one (chain.archive), carries `(chain: decision)` tags (nine today) and has no chain end step, so no tag meaning; (2) apply and address-reviews carry `(chain: not a prompt)` tags, which CHAIN_TAG_MEANING (today's bytes) does not explain, although R-rop-6 names four tags and the delta lists three. Narrow the sentence to what this change makes true, or make it true.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Narrow the delta: the five chaining bodies explain the three prompt tags (`target`, `routine`, `decision`) through their basic content, archive's tags take their meaning from the arriving session's chain end step, and `(chain: not a prompt)` is named as self-describing. Record the narrowing against R-rop-6's four tags.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Make the closure true: add a sentence on `(chain: not a prompt)` to the chain end basic content (outside CHAIN_TAG_MEANING, so its bytes hold), and carry the tag meaning in archive's body too, re-measuring the size table. This takes on more than the drafted stage.

findings.title: No task covers the stage's second exit criterion: the three stage-D steps' usual results handled by the basic content, shown by test
findings.recommendation: The program doc's stage conditional-steps has this exit criterion: 'For the three steps from stage D, the usual result (every reviewed gate passed or superseded, no fingerprint diverged, no size breach) is handled by the basic content, shown by test.' Task 6.2 tests only the default-off results (`action: off`, `configured: false`, `why: "off"`, `ceiling: null`). Nothing tests the gate rows all passed or superseded, `orbit fingerprint --check` all `verified`, or a size check that is on with empty `breaches`. Extend 6.2, or add a task, for these three cases in a disposable project: each command returns the usual result, and the archive and propose basic contents name that result as the one they handle without reading their reference file.

findings.title: The six new 'reads no reference file' scenarios assert session behaviour that no planned test can observe
findings.recommendation: Each new scenario (two in orbit-conventions, one each in archive, architect and propose) has a THEN of the form 'the session reads no references/<file>.md', which is agent behaviour. D-cs-7 makes the stage tests-only, and tasks 2.2 and 3.4 just say 'tag the delta scenarios'. A `text` tag on the generated body would claim more than its test asserts, so two implementers would tag them differently. Either reword each THEN to the property the tests check, or declare these scenarios with a scenario-ledger entry naming D-cs-7's limit, and say which in tasks 2.2 and 3.4.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Reword each THEN to the generated-text property the tests check: the body's basic content handles <result> with no step, and names the reference file only for the other results. Tag them `text`.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Keep the behavioural THENs and declare them through scenario-ledger entries that cite D-cs-7, as session behaviour not shown by test. Name this in tasks 2.2 and 3.4.

findings.title: Where propose's and ff's moved Position paragraphs land in the shared pr-choreography.md, and how far each moved block reaches, are unspecified
findings.recommendation: PR_CHOREOGRAPHY_REFERENCE is one text shipped to both propose and ff, so it will carry both paragraphs, whose step names differ: phase 3 runs after Step 0d's move at propose and after Step 5's final status at ff. Say where in the reference they go (under Phase 1, or a new section), how each is labelled for its skill, and whether the bold label '(NEW Step 0.5 — this section is placed last for reading, not for running)' moves with its paragraph. Task 1.1 hashes the block, so its extent decides the hash.

findings.title: Byte-equal moves carry positional pointers that are wrong in their new homes; Risks names only one
findings.recommendation: Risks accepts the architect save paragraph's 'no row below reads them'. The same thing happens elsewhere: SIGNOFF_HOLD_STEP says 'the save's outcome being the save step's just above', but in signoff-hold.md the save stays in the archive body's Step 3.6 (bulk-archive keeps the constant, so its bytes cannot change); the size brief says 'REPLACES the completion prompt to review (below)', and in size-brief.md nothing follows; and the propose and ff Position labels say 'placed last for reading' if they move. Name these in the same Risks entry, so stage C's tightening finds them.

findings.title: The commit and chain end basic contents phrase their exits less precisely than the full steps and the hold basic contents
findings.recommendation: The commit basic content says 'before the position readout', and COMMIT_STEP adds '(in archive, the completion readout)'. Both the commit and chain end basic contents say 'On any other result', and the commit delta says explicitly 'a non-zero exit included', as the archive and architect hold basic contents do ('On any other result or a non-zero exit'). Use the same words in all of them, so the non-zero exit is visibly routed to the reference.

findings.title: 'Seven steps' is followed by eight bullets and design §1's 'The seven splits' has eight rows
findings.recommendation: The program doc counts the sign-off hold as one step carried by two bodies. The proposal and design list archive's and architect's holds separately, so a reader counts eight. Say 'seven steps (the sign-off hold in archive and architect)', or merge the two rows. The design's size table also mixes '3,504' with '17604'.

commentary: Probed hard: the five MODIFIED blocks were word-diffed against their baselines (clean: every baseline scenario carried, only the two-halves statements and one new scenario each added). Each drafted basic content was compared with the live constant or template text it replaces (COMMIT_STEP, CHAIN_END_STEP, SIGNOFF_HOLD_STEP, PROGRAM_SIGNOFF_STEP, archive Steps 3.4 and 3.45, the size brief, the PR Position paragraphs). Every test that pins moved text was listed (test/core/pr/commit-step.test.ts and pr-references.test.ts do not need retargeting). The design's size arithmetic was recomputed (the saves sum to 47,130), the README and supported-tools count was checked against the installed surface (14 skills hold references/, onboard none), and the 500-line limit was checked against today's bodies (only explore exceeds it). The pattern behind the findings is one thing: moving text byte-equal is safe for the text itself, but the ORDER of reading changes. A rule that today sits beside the read it governs (the chained read's flags) now comes after that read, and a closure stated about the bodies ('no tag unexplained') was carried from R-rop-6 into a requirement without being measured against archive's and apply's tags. The decomposition, the composed-once constants and the block-hash test are sound.

direction.reasoning: The stage's shape is right: one constant per moved block, a recorded hash before any edit, basic content that branches on a command result rather than on judgement, and the budget test landing on day-one-true limits. What needs settling before apply is local to the design, the orbit-conventions delta and the tasks: the chained read must keep its flags, the tag closure must be narrowed or made true, and the second exit criterion needs a task. None of it reopens a ratified scope decision. Walk these and go on to apply.
